text:
The strongest matching taxonomy is [TREC Product Recommendation 2025](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html): distinguish functional substitutes, complements, merely related items, and irrelevance; separately label compatibility as supported, unknown, or incompatible. This directly addresses broad resemblance without useful function and prevents missing specifications from becoming false incompatibility judgments. Purchase redundancy needs a separate, context-dependent probe: a substitute for a previously purchased item may be redundant, but history alone cannot establish replacement, replenishment, or gift intent.

For evidence-grounded annotation, a practical adaptation is to record each proposed failure, the supporting history events and title/description spans, and an explicit “insufficient evidence” outcome. Require stated model/interface specifications for compatibility claims; treat textual similarity as a screening signal rather than proof of personal relevance. [PROVE-REC (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02968) explores verifiable preference evidence, although its use of reviews exceeds this task’s available inputs. Here, restrict evidence to histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps; leave unobserved preferences and simulator traits unknown.

Validate these proposed probes against available real-user judgments before treating them as reliable diagnostics. Report per-failure precision/recall, annotation agreement, and abstention coverage; keep uncertain identification separate from explicit rejection. [Trust or Escalate (ICLR 2025)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/08dabd5345b37fffcbe335bd578b15a0-Paper-Conference.pdf) supports confidence-calibrated selective judging against human agreement. [Rating Indeterminacy (NeurIPS 2025)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/a309239c11a28c597d050bd4a1752d32-Abstract-Conference.html) warns that forced choices can distort validation when judgments are ambiguous. These are auxiliary diagnostics; retain macro validation HR@10 for model selection.
